title: Merge two binary trees
label: idb-list
statement: Overlay two binary trees. Where both trees have a node in the same position, the merged node holds the **sum** of their values; where only one has a node, the merged tree keeps it. Return the merged tree **without changing either input**.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 617 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it is a variation of InterviewDB Q17. The binary case of Q17: overlap and the values are summed, otherwise the non-null node is used. Q17 generalises it in the direction that matters - children identified by key rather than by position, so child lookup becomes a dictionary probe and "absent branch" becomes a real case. Reader-reported, and the reader’s own note already describes the n-ary keyed variant.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Overlay two binary trees. Where both trees have a node in the same position, the merged node holds the **sum** of their values; where only one has a node, the merged tree keeps it. Return the merged tree **without changing either input**.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- New tree or modify one input? (New tree — say what you choose and why.)
- Shared nodes allowed in the result? (No — a later change would leak into the input.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Recurse on matching positions. Both present → new node with the sum. One missing → copy the other subtree. LeetCode's own answer reuses the existing subtree instead of copying; that is faster but makes the result share nodes with an input, which a caller can trip over.
